messages:
Maria: heads up — canary eval run on nightly-models shows a sharp drop in mean_response_quality for gptx-7b-q4. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/ev/plots/2026-03-20 :eyes:
Ajay: link? severity?
Maria: mean_response_quality fell from 0.78 -> 0.52 on the canary slice (same prompts). CI canary job finished green tho, which is weird.
ci-bot: Canary eval job #ev-921 finished: status=SUCCESS, artifacts -> s3://redwood-ev/canaries/ev-921
eval-bot: Metric diff summary: mean_response_quality: -0.26, embed-sim: -0.03, det-bleu: -0.02
Lucy: hmm runner telemetry vs reporting mismatch possible. saw this before when runner bumped batching kernel. Maria can you paste the eval command you ran?
Maria: sure — ran locally with the harness: 
```
python ev_run.py --model gptx-7b-q4 --suite canary_regressions --seed 42 --timeout 300
```
Outputs attached in the artifacts link but here are the head diffs: 
```
- mean_response_quality: 0.78
+ mean_response_quality: 0.52
```
Ajay: do we have per-run logs from the runner? maybe quant kernel falling back or KV cache eviction.
Lucy: pulled runner logs: there's a line around 14:02: 
```
WARN kernel_selector: fallback to generic_kernel for attn_seq=2048, reason=missing_optimized_kernel
```
and then metric emission shows mean_response_quality=0.63 inside runner events, but reporting pipeline shows 0.52. So two hypotheses: (1) runner emitted different aggregated buckets vs reporting sampling, (2) post-processing in reporting messed up.
Samir: Also note we merged PR #4523 yesterday which changed continuous-batch timeout and kv-eviction threshold. Suspect it may drop KV hits for long prompts and degrade outputs.
Jin: commit 9f2b7a4 in runtime: 
```
commit 9f2b7a4
Author: runtime-ops
Change: lower kv_cache_ttl from 60s -> 5s to free memory faster
```
That could cause more re-computation and worse quality for some prompted contexts.
Maria: I re-ran a small subset forcing kv_cache_ttl=60 locally and got mean_response_quality back to ~0.76. So that strongly points to kv eviction.
Ajay: good repro. Is the canary cluster running the new runtime?
Lucy: yes, canary nodes have the runtime build with 9f2b7a4. Production still on previous build (for now).
Samir: action items: (A) Hold rollout of runtime change for Dedicated/Dedicated canary to prod, (B) revert or patch quick fix to restore kv_cache_ttl, (C) run a targeted bisect across PRs touching runtime + batcher.
Maria: I'll open an emergency PR reverting the kv change and run canary eval.
Ajay: also add a test in eval-harness that exercises long-context cache hits — we lack a guard test for this.
Jin: agree. I'll draft the revert now. If we want minimal risk, we can flip the config flag back without full revert: 
```
runtime.flags.kv_cache_ttl=60
```
Samir: +1 on config flip first, revert if that doesn't resolve. We need to move fast.
ci-bot: Deploy pipeline: canary-runtime v2.14 -> queued for deploy to canary nodes. Cancel?
Maria: Cancel deploy and block rollout until config flip applied. @Ajay can you temporarily block the canary target?
Ajay: done, rolled back canary target to v2.13 and cancelled v2.14 deploy.
Maria: PR #4598 opened: "revert: kv_cache_ttl quick flip" — deploying config patch to canary now and kicking eval run.
ci-bot: Deploy config-patch PR-4598 -> canary: started
eval-bot: new canary eval started: ev-922
Maria: ev-922 finished — mean_response_quality back to 0.75 on the same slice.
Lucy: amazing. That confirms runtime config was root cause. We should still run a short bisect across recent PRs to make sure no other perf regressions slipped in. But we can unblock rollout with config change and follow up with full revert if needed.
Samir: I'll log an incident ticket and assign postmortem. Also add a gating test for kv-cache in eval-ci.
Jin: I'll put up an RFC to rework eviction strategy with better telemetry (cache-hit-rate histogram) so this doesn't surprise reporting.
Maria: thanks everyone. I'll leave the canary pinned until we have the bisect results and the follow-up test.
Ajay: noted. If anyone wants to dig into detailed logs I put the runner traces here: https://internal.redwood/traces/ev-922/trace.log
Maria: closing thread for now, but please add any findings to the incident ticket I created: INC-2026-0312
Samir: added timeline and next steps. :white_check_mark:
